-- arxiv / shared helpers (inlined at build time — the sandbox has no require)
--
-- No auth: arXiv's public API is credential-free. Politeness lives in the
-- command structure: one query per invocation (the sandbox has no sleep,
-- so the caller's cadence IS the throttle — Sept 13 brownout lesson from
-- the original fetcher). UA etiquette: identify the client honestly.
--
-- Lua-pattern note: `.` does not cross newlines — every multi-line span
-- below uses [%s%S] (matches everything) with lazy `-%b-` semantics.

local shared = {}

shared.UA = "animus-arxiv-package/0.1.0 (agent reading cache; contact via arxiv user)"
shared.API = "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query"
shared.HTML_BASE = "https://arxiv.org/html/"
shared.PDF_BASE = "https://arxiv.org/pdf/"

function shared.headers()
  return { ["User-Agent"] = shared.UA }
end

-- Old-style ids contain '/' (hep-th/9901001) — the fs namespace is slug-only.
function shared.safe_id(id)
  return string.gsub(tostring(id), "/", "_")
end

-- Error string for a failed HTTP result. A bare status hides the transport
-- reason: r.error carries curl's verdict; without it a stall reads as a
-- meaningless "HTTP 0" (alpaca Sept 14 lesson, shared blood).
function shared.http_error(r)
  local s = "HTTP " .. tostring(r.status)
  if r.error ~= nil and r.error ~= "" then
    s = s .. " (" .. tostring(r.error) .. ")"
  end
  return s
end

-- HTML entity decode: the named set plus numeric forms. utf8.char may be
-- absent in the sandbox (defensively guarded); numeric entities then fall
-- through undecoded — readable, not pretty.
function shared.decode_entities(s)
  if s == nil then return "" end
  s = string.gsub(s, "&", "&")
  s = string.gsub(s, "<", "<")
  s = string.gsub(s, ">", ">")
  s = string.gsub(s, """, '"')
  s = string.gsub(s, "'", "'")
  s = string.gsub(s, "'", "'")
  s = string.gsub(s, " ", " ")
  if utf8 ~= nil and utf8.char ~= nil then
    s = string.gsub(s, "&#x(%x+);", function(h) return utf8.char(tonumber(h, 16)) end)
    s = string.gsub(s, "&#(%d+);", function(d) return utf8.char(tonumber(d)) end)
  end
  return s
end

-- Tag inner text (title/summary span lines; tolerate line-broken markup).
function shared.tag(block, name)
  local v = string.match(block, "<" .. name .. "[^>]*>[%s%S]-</" .. name .. ">")
  if v == nil then return nil end
  v = string.gsub(v, "^<" .. name .. "[^>]*>", "")
  v = string.gsub(v, "</" .. name .. ">$", "")
  v = string.gsub(v, "<[^>]*>", "")
  v = string.gsub(v, "%s+", " ")
  v = string.gsub(v, "^%s", "")
  v = string.gsub(v, "%s$", "")
  return shared.decode_entities(v)
end

-- Parse an arXiv Atom feed into entries:
-- {id, title, authors[], summary, published, pdf_url, categories[], primary_category, abs_url}
function shared.atom_parse(xml)
  local entries = {}
  if xml == nil then return entries end
  for block in string.gmatch(xml, "<entry>[%s%S]-</entry>") do
    local e = {}
    local raw_id = shared.tag(block, "id") or ""
    e.id = string.match(raw_id, "/abs/([^%s]+)") or raw_id
    e.title = shared.tag(block, "title") or ""
    e.authors = {}
    for name in string.gmatch(block, "<name>([%s%S]-)</name>") do
      table.insert(e.authors, shared.decode_entities(string.gsub(name, "%s+", " ")))
    end
    e.summary = shared.tag(block, "summary") or ""
    local pub = string.match(block, "<published>([^<]+)</published>")
    e.published = pub and string.sub(pub, 1, 10) or ""
    e.pdf_url = nil
    for href in string.gmatch(block, '<link[^>]-title="pdf"[^>]-href="([^"]*)"') do
      e.pdf_url = href
    end
    for href in string.gmatch(block, '<link[^>]-href="([^"]*)"[^>]-title="pdf"') do
      e.pdf_url = href
    end
    e.categories = {}
    for term in string.gmatch(block, '<category term="([^"]*)"') do
      table.insert(e.categories, term)
    end
    e.primary_category = string.match(block, 'primary_category term="([^"]*)"')
      or (e.categories[1] or "")
    e.abs_url = "https://arxiv.org/abs/" .. e.id
    table.insert(entries, e)
  end
  return entries
end

-- Compact an entry for tool results: full identity, trimmed summary.
function shared.compact(e, summary_chars)
  local limit = summary_chars or 400
  local authors = {}
  for i = 1, math.min(3, #e.authors) do authors[i] = e.authors[i] end
  if #e.authors > 3 then authors[#authors + 1] = "et al." end
  local summary = e.summary or ""
  if #summary > limit then summary = string.sub(summary, 1, limit) .. "…" end
  return {
    id = e.id, title = e.title, authors = authors, published = e.published,
    primary_category = e.primary_category, summary = summary, pdf_url = e.pdf_url
  }
end

-- Compile an agent-supplied query into arXiv search syntax.
-- Expert mode: any field prefix (cat:, ti:, abs:, all:…), boolean
-- operator, or parenthesis → VERBATIM passthrough. Fixes the cat: bug
-- (Buffett field report #1): 'cat:q-fin.CP' wrapped as all:cat:q-fin.CP
-- → HTTP 400.
-- Simple mode: terms and quoted phrases AND-joined as all: fields.
-- Fixes the silent-OR bug (Buffett #2): arXiv rewrites space-separated
-- terms as implicit OR — 'sovereign default credit supply' returned the
-- latest-indexed papers from random fields (feed-echo witness:
-- 'all:sovereign OR all:default OR all:credit OR all:supply'). AND is
-- the overwhelming intent; OR stays available via expert mode.
function shared.compile_query(query)
  query = tostring(query)
  local expert = string.find(query, ":", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, " AND ", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, " OR ", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, "ANDNOT", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, "(", 1, true) ~= nil
  if expert then return query end
  local terms = {}
  local rest = string.gsub(query, '"([^"]*)"', function(p)
    if #p > 0 then terms[#terms + 1] = 'all:"' .. p .. '"' end
    return " "
  end)
  for w in string.gmatch(rest, "%S+") do
    terms[#terms + 1] = "all:" .. w
  end
  return table.concat(terms, " AND ")
end

-- The feed's own <title> echoes the query the API actually executed
-- ('arXiv Query: search_query=…'). Surfacing it in results makes any
-- server-side query rewrite VISIBLE — the observability that would
-- have made the silent-OR bug self-evident.
function shared.feed_query(xml)
  if xml == nil then return nil end
  local t = shared.tag(xml, "title")
  if t == nil then return nil end
  local q = string.match(t, "search_query=(.-)&id_list")
  if q == nil then q = string.match(t, "search_query=(.*)") end
  return q
end

-- URL-encode a compiled query: space → '+' (arXiv's separator form),
-- everything outside unreserved (+ and " exempt) percent-encoded.
function shared.query_url(query, start, max_results, sort)
  local compiled = shared.compile_query(query)
  local esc = string.gsub(compiled, " ", "+")
  esc = string.gsub(esc, '([^%w%-%.%_%~%+"])', function(c)
    return string.format("%%%02X", string.byte(c))
  end)
  local url = shared.API .. "?search_query=" .. esc ..
    "&start=" .. tostring(start or 0) ..
    "&max_results=" .. tostring(max_results or 10)
  if sort ~= nil and sort ~= "" then
    url = url .. "&sortBy=" .. tostring(sort) .. "&sortOrder=descending"
  end
  return url
end

function shared.id_url(id)
  local esc = string.gsub(tostring(id), "([^%w%-%.%_%~])", function(c)
    return string.format("%%%02X", string.byte(c))
  end)
  return shared.API .. "?id_list=" .. esc .. "&max_results=1"
end

-- Block-close tag classification for strip_html.
local para_tags = { p = true, div = true, section = true, article = true,
  figure = true, table = true, blockquote = true, figcaption = true,
  ul = true, ol = true, dt = true, dd = true }
for i = 1, 6 do para_tags["h" .. i] = true end
local line_tags = { li = true, tr = true, td = true, th = true }

-- HTML → text. LaTeXML renderings: math alttext kept inline as $...$ LaTeX
-- (agents read LaTeX better than stripped glyphs), script/style/head and
-- comments dropped, block closes become paragraph breaks, entities decoded.
function shared.strip_html(html)
  if html == nil then return "" end
  -- arXiv LaTeXML renderings wrap the paper in exactly ONE <article> span;
  -- everything outside it is site chrome (report-issue forms, banners,
  -- nav, footers — the live 2607 page carried more than the fixture did).
  -- Prefer the article span; fall back to explicit chrome-block removal.
  local art = string.match(html, "<article[^>]*>[%s%S]-</article>")
  if art ~= nil then
    html = art
  else
    html = string.gsub(html, "<nav[^>]*>[%s%S]-</nav>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<header[^>]*>[%s%S]-</header>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<footer[^>]*>[%s%S]-</footer>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<form[^>]*>[%s%S]-</form>", " ")
  end
  html = string.gsub(html, "<script[%s%S]-</script>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<style[%s%S]-</style>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<head[^>]*>[%s%S]-</head>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<!%-%-[%s%S]-%-%->", " ")
  -- math: keep the LaTeX alttext inline if present (position-independent),
  -- then drop the whole <math>...</math> span (LaTeXML never nests math)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<math([^>]*)>[%s%S]-</math>", function(attrs)
    local alt = string.match(attrs, 'alttext="([^"]*)"')
    if alt ~= nil then return " $" .. shared.decode_entities(alt) .. "$ " end
    return " "
  end)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<annotation[%s%S]-</annotation>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<svg[%s%S]-</svg>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<img[%s%S]->", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<br[%s%S]->", "\n")
  -- block closes → breaks (before generic strip; inserted text has no '<')
  html = string.gsub(html, "</(%a+)[^>]->", function(tag)
    tag = string.lower(tag)
    if para_tags[tag] then return "\n\n" end
    if line_tags[tag] then return "\n" end
    return " "
  end)
  -- remaining tags stripped (lazy to first '>' — raw '>' never appears inside a tag)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<[%s%S]->", "")
  html = shared.decode_entities(html)
  -- collapse: space runs → one; blank-line runs → one blank line; trim ends
  html = string.gsub(html, "[ \t]+", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, " *\n *", "\n")
  html = string.gsub(html, "\n\n\n+", "\n\n")
  html = string.gsub(html, "^\n+", "")
  html = string.gsub(html, "\n+$", "")
  return html
end

-- Split text into pages of at most max_bytes, breaking at (in priority)
-- the last paragraph seam, newline, sentence end, or space in the window.
-- Returns {pages = {...}, total_chars = n}. Terminates: brk >= 1 always.
function shared.split_pages(text, max_bytes)
  local cap = max_bytes or 8192
  local pages = {}
  local pos, n = 1, #text
  while pos <= n do
    if n - pos + 1 <= cap then
      local last = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos), "^%s+", "")
      if #last > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = last end
      break
    end
    local window = string.sub(text, pos, pos + cap - 1)
    local brk = nil
    -- last paragraph seam
    local i = #window - 1
    while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
      if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" and string.sub(window, i + 1, i + 1) == "\n" then brk = i end
      i = i - 1
    end
    -- last single newline
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last sentence end
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 2 and brk == nil do
        local prev = string.sub(window, i - 1, i - 1)
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " and (prev == "." or prev == "!") then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last space
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    if brk == nil or brk < 1 then brk = cap end
    local chunk = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos, pos + brk - 1), "%s+$", "")
    if #chunk > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = chunk end
    pos = pos + brk
    while pos <= n do
      local c = string.sub(text, pos, pos)
      if c == "\n" or c == " " or c == "\t" then pos = pos + 1 else break end
    end
  end
  if #pages == 0 then pages[1] = "" end
  return { pages = pages, total_chars = n }
end

-- Load a JSON-array state key defensively (nil/""/invalid → fallback).
function shared.load_json_state(ctx, key, fallback)
  local raw = ctx.package.get_state(key)
  if raw == nil or raw == "" or raw == "***" then return fallback end
  local ok, v = pcall(json.decode_safe, raw)
  if not ok or type(v) ~= "table" then return fallback end
  return v
end

-- The library index lives in state as a JSON object keyed by arxiv id.
function shared.load_library(ctx)
  local lib = shared.load_json_state(ctx, "library", {})
  return lib
end

-- Delete all filespace artifacts of a cached paper (library entry shape).
function shared.remove_files(ctx, sid, entry)
  local n = tonumber(entry.pages) or 0
  for i = 1, n do
    ctx.fs.delete(string.format("%s-p%03d.txt", sid, i))
  end
  ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".meta.json")
  if entry.has_pdf then ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".pdf") end
end


function run(ctx)
  local a = ctx.args
  if a.query == nil or a.query == "" then
    return {success = false, error = "query required (e.g. 'electron correlation lattice')"}
  end
  local r = ctx.http.get(
    shared.query_url(a.query, a.start, a.max_results, a.sort),
    {headers = shared.headers()})
  if r.status ~= 200 then
    return {success = false, error = "search failed: " .. shared.http_error(r)}
  end
  local entries = shared.atom_parse(r.body)
  local out = {}
  for _, e in ipairs(entries) do out[#out + 1] = shared.compact(e) end
  return {success = true, count = #entries, results = out,
          executed_query = shared.feed_query(r.body)}
end

-- comments dropped, block closes become paragraph breaks, entities decoded.
function shared.strip_html(html)
  if html == nil then return "" end
  -- arXiv LaTeXML renderings wrap the paper in exactly ONE <article> span;
  -- everything outside it is site chrome (report-issue forms, banners,
  -- nav, footers — the live 2607 page carried more than the fixture did).
  -- Prefer the article span; fall back to explicit chrome-block removal.
  local art = string.match(html, "<article[^>]*>[%s%S]-</article>")
  if art ~= nil then
    html = art
  else
    html = string.gsub(html, "<nav[^>]*>[%s%S]-</nav>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<header[^>]*>[%s%S]-</header>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<footer[^>]*>[%s%S]-</footer>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<form[^>]*>[%s%S]-</form>", " ")
  end
  html = string.gsub(html, "<script[%s%S]-</script>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<style[%s%S]-</style>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<head[^>]*>[%s%S]-</head>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<!%-%-[%s%S]-%-%->", " ")
  -- math: keep the LaTeX alttext inline if present (position-independent),
  -- then drop the whole <math>...</math> span (LaTeXML never nests math)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<math([^>]*)>[%s%S]-</math>", function(attrs)
    local alt = string.match(attrs, 'alttext="([^"]*)"')
    if alt ~= nil then return " $" .. shared.decode_entities(alt) .. "$ " end
    return " "
  end)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<annotation[%s%S]-</annotation>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<svg[%s%S]-</svg>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<img[%s%S]->", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<br[%s%S]->", "\n")
  -- block closes → breaks (before generic strip; inserted text has no '<')
  html = string.gsub(html, "</(%a+)[^>]->", function(tag)
    tag = string.lower(tag)
    if para_tags[tag] then return "\n\n" end
    if line_tags[tag] then return "\n" end
    return " "
  end)
  -- remaining tags stripped (lazy to first '>' — raw '>' never appears inside a tag)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<[%s%S]->", "")
  html = shared.decode_entities(html)
  -- collapse: space runs → one; blank-line runs → one blank line; trim ends
  html = string.gsub(html, "[ \t]+", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, " *\n *", "\n")
  html = string.gsub(html, "\n\n\n+", "\n\n")
  html = string.gsub(html, "^\n+", "")
  html = string.gsub(html, "\n+$", "")
  return html
end

-- Split text into pages of at most max_bytes, breaking at (in priority)
-- the last paragraph seam, newline, sentence end, or space in the window.
-- Returns {pages = {...}, total_chars = n}. Terminates: brk >= 1 always.
function shared.split_pages(text, max_bytes)
  local cap = max_bytes or 8192
  local pages = {}
  local pos, n = 1, #text
  while pos <= n do
    if n - pos + 1 <= cap then
      local last = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos), "^%s+", "")
      if #last > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = last end
      break
    end
    local window = string.sub(text, pos, pos + cap - 1)
    local brk = nil
    -- last paragraph seam
    local i = #window - 1
    while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
      if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" and string.sub(window, i + 1, i + 1) == "\n" then brk = i end
      i = i - 1
    end
    -- last single newline
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last sentence end
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 2 and brk == nil do
        local prev = string.sub(window, i - 1, i - 1)
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " and (prev == "." or prev == "!") then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last space
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    if brk == nil or brk < 1 then brk = cap end
    local chunk = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos, pos + brk - 1), "%s+$", "")
    if #chunk > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = chunk end
    pos = pos + brk
    while pos <= n do
      local c = string.sub(text, pos, pos)
      if c == "\n" or c == " " or c == "\t" then pos = pos + 1 else break end
    end
  end
  if #pages == 0 then pages[1] = "" end
  return { pages = pages, total_chars = n }
end

-- Load a JSON-array state key defensively (nil/""/invalid → fallback).
function shared.load_json_state(ctx, key, fallback)
  local raw = ctx.package.get_state(key)
  if raw == nil or raw == "" or raw == "***" then return fallback end
  local ok, v = pcall(json.decode_safe, raw)
  if not ok or type(v) ~= "table" then return fallback end
  return v
end

-- The library index lives in state as a JSON object keyed by arxiv id.
function shared.load_library(ctx)
  local lib = shared.load_json_state(ctx, "library", {})
  return lib
end

-- Delete all filespace artifacts of a cached paper (library entry shape).
function shared.remove_files(ctx, sid, entry)
  local n = tonumber(entry.pages) or 0
  for i = 1, n do
    ctx.fs.delete(string.format("%s-p%03d.txt", sid, i))
  end
  ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".meta.json")
  if entry.has_pdf then ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".pdf") end
end


-- paper abstract: full metadata + abstract for any paper, no cache required.
function run(ctx)
  local a = ctx.args
  if a.id == nil or a.id == "" then
    return {success = false, error = "id required (e.g. 2401.12345)"}
  end
  local r = ctx.http.get(shared.id_url(a.id), {headers = shared.headers()})
  if r.status ~= 200 then
    return {success = false, error = "fetch failed: " .. shared.http_error(r)}
  end
  local entries = shared.atom_parse(r.body)
  local e = entries[1]
  if e == nil then
    return {success = false, error = "no arxiv entry for id '" .. tostring(a.id) .. "'"}
  end
  return {
    success = true, id = e.id, title = e.title, authors = e.authors,
    published = e.published, categories = e.categories,
    primary_category = e.primary_category, summary = e.summary,
    pdf_url = e.pdf_url, abs_url = e.abs_url,
    hint = "run 'paper cache' to fetch the full text for paginated reading"
  }
end

commands.name: paper cache
commands.description: Cache a paper for reading: fetch metadata, pull the arXiv HTML rendering, strip to text, split into ~8KB pages in the package filespace. Falls back to abstract-only when no rendering exists. Re-caching replaces the old copy. include_pdf=true also archives the PDF binary.
commands.script:
-- arxiv / shared helpers (inlined at build time — the sandbox has no require)
--
-- No auth: arXiv's public API is credential-free. Politeness lives in the
-- command structure: one query per invocation (the sandbox has no sleep,
-- so the caller's cadence IS the throttle — Sept 13 brownout lesson from
-- the original fetcher). UA etiquette: identify the client honestly.
--
-- Lua-pattern note: `.` does not cross newlines — every multi-line span
-- below uses [%s%S] (matches everything) with lazy `-%b-` semantics.

local shared = {}

shared.UA = "animus-arxiv-package/0.1.0 (agent reading cache; contact via arxiv user)"
shared.API = "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query"
shared.HTML_BASE = "https://arxiv.org/html/"
shared.PDF_BASE = "https://arxiv.org/pdf/"

function shared.headers()
  return { ["User-Agent"] = shared.UA }
end

-- Old-style ids contain '/' (hep-th/9901001) — the fs namespace is slug-only.
function shared.safe_id(id)
  return string.gsub(tostring(id), "/", "_")
end

-- Error string for a failed HTTP result. A bare status hides the transport
-- reason: r.error carries curl's verdict; without it a stall reads as a
-- meaningless "HTTP 0" (alpaca Sept 14 lesson, shared blood).
function shared.http_error(r)
  local s = "HTTP " .. tostring(r.status)
  if r.error ~= nil and r.error ~= "" then
    s = s .. " (" .. tostring(r.error) .. ")"
  end
  return s
end

-- HTML entity decode: the named set plus numeric forms. utf8.char may be
-- absent in the sandbox (defensively guarded); numeric entities then fall
-- through undecoded — readable, not pretty.
function shared.decode_entities(s)
  if s == nil then return "" end
  s = string.gsub(s, "&", "&")
  s = string.gsub(s, "<", "<")
  s = string.gsub(s, ">", ">")
  s = string.gsub(s, """, '"')
  s = string.gsub(s, "'", "'")
  s = string.gsub(s, "'", "'")
  s = string.gsub(s, " ", " ")
  if utf8 ~= nil and utf8.char ~= nil then
    s = string.gsub(s, "&#x(%x+);", function(h) return utf8.char(tonumber(h, 16)) end)
    s = string.gsub(s, "&#(%d+);", function(d) return utf8.char(tonumber(d)) end)
  end
  return s
end

-- Tag inner text (title/summary span lines; tolerate line-broken markup).
function shared.tag(block, name)
  local v = string.match(block, "<" .. name .. "[^>]*>[%s%S]-</" .. name .. ">")
  if v == nil then return nil end
  v = string.gsub(v, "^<" .. name .. "[^>]*>", "")
  v = string.gsub(v, "</" .. name .. ">$", "")
  v = string.gsub(v, "<[^>]*>", "")
  v = string.gsub(v, "%s+", " ")
  v = string.gsub(v, "^%s", "")
  v = string.gsub(v, "%s$", "")
  return shared.decode_entities(v)
end

-- Parse an arXiv Atom feed into entries:
-- {id, title, authors[], summary, published, pdf_url, categories[], primary_category, abs_url}
function shared.atom_parse(xml)
  local entries = {}
  if xml == nil then return entries end
  for block in string.gmatch(xml, "<entry>[%s%S]-</entry>") do
    local e = {}
    local raw_id = shared.tag(block, "id") or ""
    e.id = string.match(raw_id, "/abs/([^%s]+)") or raw_id
    e.title = shared.tag(block, "title") or ""
    e.authors = {}
    for name in string.gmatch(block, "<name>([%s%S]-)</name>") do
      table.insert(e.authors, shared.decode_entities(string.gsub(name, "%s+", " ")))
    end
    e.summary = shared.tag(block, "summary") or ""
    local pub = string.match(block, "<published>([^<]+)</published>")
    e.published = pub and string.sub(pub, 1, 10) or ""
    e.pdf_url = nil
    for href in string.gmatch(block, '<link[^>]-title="pdf"[^>]-href="([^"]*)"') do
      e.pdf_url = href
    end
    for href in string.gmatch(block, '<link[^>]-href="([^"]*)"[^>]-title="pdf"') do
      e.pdf_url = href
    end
    e.categories = {}
    for term in string.gmatch(block, '<category term="([^"]*)"') do
      table.insert(e.categories, term)
    end
    e.primary_category = string.match(block, 'primary_category term="([^"]*)"')
      or (e.categories[1] or "")
    e.abs_url = "https://arxiv.org/abs/" .. e.id
    table.insert(entries, e)
  end
  return entries
end

-- Compact an entry for tool results: full identity, trimmed summary.
function shared.compact(e, summary_chars)
  local limit = summary_chars or 400
  local authors = {}
  for i = 1, math.min(3, #e.authors) do authors[i] = e.authors[i] end
  if #e.authors > 3 then authors[#authors + 1] = "et al." end
  local summary = e.summary or ""
  if #summary > limit then summary = string.sub(summary, 1, limit) .. "…" end
  return {
    id = e.id, title = e.title, authors = authors, published = e.published,
    primary_category = e.primary_category, summary = summary, pdf_url = e.pdf_url
  }
end

-- Compile an agent-supplied query into arXiv search syntax.
-- Expert mode: any field prefix (cat:, ti:, abs:, all:…), boolean
-- operator, or parenthesis → VERBATIM passthrough. Fixes the cat: bug
-- (Buffett field report #1): 'cat:q-fin.CP' wrapped as all:cat:q-fin.CP
-- → HTTP 400.
-- Simple mode: terms and quoted phrases AND-joined as all: fields.
-- Fixes the silent-OR bug (Buffett #2): arXiv rewrites space-separated
-- terms as implicit OR — 'sovereign default credit supply' returned the
-- latest-indexed papers from random fields (feed-echo witness:
-- 'all:sovereign OR all:default OR all:credit OR all:supply'). AND is
-- the overwhelming intent; OR stays available via expert mode.
function shared.compile_query(query)
  query = tostring(query)
  local expert = string.find(query, ":", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, " AND ", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, " OR ", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, "ANDNOT", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, "(", 1, true) ~= nil
  if expert then return query end
  local terms = {}
  local rest = string.gsub(query, '"([^"]*)"', function(p)
    if #p > 0 then terms[#terms + 1] = 'all:"' .. p .. '"' end
    return " "
  end)
  for w in string.gmatch(rest, "%S+") do
    terms[#terms + 1] = "all:" .. w
  end
  return table.concat(terms, " AND ")
end

-- The feed's own <title> echoes the query the API actually executed
-- ('arXiv Query: search_query=…'). Surfacing it in results makes any
-- server-side query rewrite VISIBLE — the observability that would
-- have made the silent-OR bug self-evident.
function shared.feed_query(xml)
  if xml == nil then return nil end
  local t = shared.tag(xml, "title")
  if t == nil then return nil end
  local q = string.match(t, "search_query=(.-)&id_list")
  if q == nil then q = string.match(t, "search_query=(.*)") end
  return q
end

-- URL-encode a compiled query: space → '+' (arXiv's separator form),
-- everything outside unreserved (+ and " exempt) percent-encoded.
function shared.query_url(query, start, max_results, sort)
  local compiled = shared.compile_query(query)
  local esc = string.gsub(compiled, " ", "+")
  esc = string.gsub(esc, '([^%w%-%.%_%~%+"])', function(c)
    return string.format("%%%02X", string.byte(c))
  end)
  local url = shared.API .. "?search_query=" .. esc ..
    "&start=" .. tostring(start or 0) ..
    "&max_results=" .. tostring(max_results or 10)
  if sort ~= nil and sort ~= "" then
    url = url .. "&sortBy=" .. tostring(sort) .. "&sortOrder=descending"
  end
  return url
end

function shared.id_url(id)
  local esc = string.gsub(tostring(id), "([^%w%-%.%_%~])", function(c)
    return string.format("%%%02X", string.byte(c))
  end)
  return shared.API .. "?id_list=" .. esc .. "&max_results=1"
end

-- Load a JSON-array state key defensively (nil/""/invalid → fallback).
function shared.load_json_state(ctx, key, fallback)

-- The library index lives in state as a JSON object keyed by arxiv id.
function shared.load_library(ctx)

  return lib
end

-- Delete all filespace artifacts of a cached paper (library entry shape).
function shared.remove_files(ctx, sid, entry)
  local n = tonumber(entry.pages) or 0
  for i = 1, n do
    ctx.fs.delete(string.format("%s-p%03d.txt", sid, i))
  end
  ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".meta.json")
  if entry.has_pdf then ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".pdf") end

-- paper cache: fetch metadata + HTML rendering, split into text pages in the
-- package filespace, index in library state. Abstract-only fallback when no
-- HTML rendering exists. Optional PDF archival.
function run(ctx)
  local a = ctx.args
  if a.id == nil or a.id == "" then
    return {success = false, error = "id required (e.g. 2401.12345 or hep-th/9901001)"}
  end

  -- 1) metadata by id (http 1/3)
  local r = ctx.http.get(shared.id_url(a.id), {headers = shared.headers()})
  if r.status ~= 200 then
    return {success = false, error = "metadata fetch failed: " .. shared.http_error(r)}
  end
  local entries = shared.atom_parse(r.body)
  local e = entries[1]
  if e == nil then
    return {success = false, error = "no arxiv entry for id '" .. tostring(a.id) ..
      "' — check the id and version (try 'paper abstract' to verify it exists)"}
  end
  local sid = shared.safe_id(e.id)

  -- 2) HTML rendering (http 2/3) — text pages; fall back to abstract-only
  local text, html_sha, mode
  local hr = ctx.http.get(shared.HTML_BASE .. e.id, {headers = shared.headers(), timeout_s = 60})
  if hr.status == 200 and #hr.body > 1000 then
    text = shared.strip_html(hr.body)
    html_sha = ctx.crypto.sha256(hr.body)
    mode = "html"
  else
    -- no rendering (or unusably short body): abstract-only cache
    text = e.title .. "\n\n" .. (e.summary or "")
    html_sha = nil
    mode = "abstract"
  end
  local sp = shared.split_pages(text, 8192)

  -- overwrite an existing cache of the same paper first (idempotent re-cache)
  local lib = shared.load_library(ctx)
  local old = lib[e.id]
  if old ~= nil then shared.remove_files(ctx, sid, old) end

  for i, ptext in ipairs(sp.pages) do
    local ok, err = ctx.fs.write(string.format("%s-p%03d.txt", sid, i), ptext)
    if not ok then
      return {success = false, error = "page write failed: " .. tostring(err) .. " (filespace quota?)"}
    end
  end

  -- 3) optional PDF archival (http 3/3) — binary; off by default
  local has_pdf = false
  if a.include_pdf and e.pdf_url ~= nil then
    local pr = ctx.http.get(e.pdf_url, {headers = shared.headers(), timeout_s = 120})
    if pr.status == 200 and #pr.body > 1000 then
      local ok, err = ctx.fs.write(sid .. ".pdf", pr.body)
      if ok then
        has_pdf = true
      else
        ctx.log("pdf cache write failed: " .. tostring(err))
      end
    else
      ctx.log("pdf fetch failed: " .. shared.http_error(pr) .. " — caching text pages only")
    end
  end

  local meta = {
    id = e.id, title = e.title, authors = e.authors, published = e.published,
    primary_category = e.primary_category, categories = e.categories,
    pdf_url = e.pdf_url, abs_url = e.abs_url,
    mode = mode, pages = #sp.pages, total_chars = sp.total_chars,

-- everything outside unreserved (+ and " exempt) percent-encoded.
function shared.query_url(query, start, max_results, sort)

  local esc = string.gsub(compiled, " ", "+")
  esc = string.gsub(esc, '([^%w%-%.%_%~%+"])', function(c)

-- comments dropped, block closes become paragraph breaks, entities decoded.
function shared.strip_html(html)
  if html == nil then return "" end

  -- nav, footers — the live 2607 page carried more than the fixture did).

  end

  html = string.gsub(html, "<style[%s%S]-</style>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<head[^>]*>[%s%S]-</head>", " ")

  -- then drop the whole <math>...</math> span (LaTeXML never nests math)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<math([^>]*)>[%s%S]-</math>", function(attrs)

  end)

  html = string.gsub(html, "</(%a+)[^>]->", function(tag)

    if line_tags[tag] then return "\n" end
    return " "
  end)

  html = string.gsub(html, "<[%s%S]->", "")
  html = shared.decode_entities(html)
  -- collapse: space runs → one; blank-line runs → one blank line; trim ends
  html = string.gsub(html, "[ \t]+", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, " *\n *", "\n")
  html = string.gsub(html, "\n\n\n+", "\n\n")
  html = string.gsub(html, "^\n+", "")
  html = string.gsub(html, "\n+$", "")
  return html

-- Split text into pages of at most max_bytes, breaking at (in priority)
-- the last paragraph seam, newline, sentence end, or space in the window.
-- Returns {pages = {...}, total_chars = n}. Terminates: brk >= 1 always.
function shared.split_pages(text, max_bytes)
  local cap = max_bytes or 8192
  local pages = {}
  local pos, n = 1, #text
  while pos <= n do
    if n - pos + 1 <= cap then
      local last = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos), "^%s+", "")
      if #last > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = last end
      break
    end
    local window = string.sub(text, pos, pos + cap - 1)
    local brk = nil
    -- last paragraph seam
    local i = #window - 1
    while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
      if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" and string.sub(window, i + 1, i + 1) == "\n" then brk = i end
      i = i - 1
    end
    -- last single newline
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last sentence end
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 2 and brk == nil do
        local prev = string.sub(window, i - 1, i - 1)
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " and (prev == "." or prev == "!") then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last space
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    if brk == nil or brk < 1 then brk = cap end
    local chunk = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos, pos + brk - 1), "%s+$", "")
    if #chunk > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = chunk end
    pos = pos + brk
    while pos <= n do
      local c = string.sub(text, pos, pos)
      if c == "\n" or c == " " or c == "\t" then pos = pos + 1 else break end
    end
  end
  if #pages == 0 then pages[1] = "" end
  return { pages = pages, total_chars = n }
end

function shared.load_json_state(ctx, key, fallback)
  local raw = ctx.package.get_state(key)
  if raw == nil or raw == "" or raw == "***" then return fallback end
  local ok, v = pcall(json.decode_safe, raw)
  if not ok or type(v) ~= "table" then return fallback end
  return v
end

-- The library index lives in state as a JSON object keyed by arxiv id.
function shared.load_library(ctx)
  local lib = shared.load_json_state(ctx, "library", {})
  return lib
end

-- Delete all filespace artifacts of a cached paper (library entry shape).
function shared.remove_files(ctx, sid, entry)
  local n = tonumber(entry.pages) or 0
  for i = 1, n do
    ctx.fs.delete(string.format("%s-p%03d.txt", sid, i))
  end
  ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".meta.json")
  if entry.has_pdf then ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".pdf") end
end


-- paper read: one page of a cached paper (paginated; 1 page ≈ 8KB text).
function run(ctx)
  local a = ctx.args
  if a.id == nil or a.id == "" then
    return {success = false, error = "id required (e.g. 2401.12345)"}
  end
  local lib = shared.load_library(ctx)
  local entry = lib[a.id]
  if entry == nil then
    -- tolerate version-less lookups for versioned cache keys
    for k, v in pairs(lib) do
      if string.sub(k, 1, #a.id) == a.id then entry = v; break end
    end
    if entry == nil then
      return {success = false, error = "not cached — run 'paper cache' first",
              id = a.id, hint = "cache list shows what's in the library"}
    end
  end
  local page = tonumber(a.page) or 1
  local total = tonumber(entry.pages) or 1
  if page < 1 or page > total then
    return {success = false, error = "page " .. page .. " out of range 1.." .. total, pages = total}
  end
  local sid = shared.safe_id(entry.id)
  local text = ctx.fs.read(string.format("%s-p%03d.txt", sid, page))
  if text == nil then
    return {success = false, error = "page file missing — cache corrupt, re-run 'paper cache'"}
  end
  local out = {
    success = true, id = entry.id, title = entry.title, mode = entry.mode,
    page = page, pages_total = total, text = text
  }
  if page < total then out.next_page = page + 1 end
  return out
end

function shared.id_url(id)
  local esc = string.gsub(tostring(id), "([^%w%-%.%_%~])", function(c)
    return string.format("%%%02X", string.byte(c))
  end)
  return shared.API .. "?id_list=" .. esc .. "&max_results=1"
end

-- Block-close tag classification for strip_html.
local para_tags = { p = true, div = true, section = true, article = true,
  figure = true, table = true, blockquote = true, figcaption = true,
  ul = true, ol = true, dt = true, dd = true }
for i = 1, 6 do para_tags["h" .. i] = true end
local line_tags = { li = true, tr = true, td = true, th = true }

-- HTML → text. LaTeXML renderings: math alttext kept inline as $...$ LaTeX
-- (agents read LaTeX better than stripped glyphs), script/style/head and
-- comments dropped, block closes become paragraph breaks, entities decoded.
function shared.strip_html(html)
  if html == nil then return "" end
  -- arXiv LaTeXML renderings wrap the paper in exactly ONE <article> span;
  -- everything outside it is site chrome (report-issue forms, banners,
  -- nav, footers — the live 2607 page carried more than the fixture did).
  -- Prefer the article span; fall back to explicit chrome-block removal.
  local art = string.match(html, "<article[^>]*>[%s%S]-</article>")
  if art ~= nil then
    html = art
  else
    html = string.gsub(html, "<nav[^>]*>[%s%S]-</nav>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<header[^>]*>[%s%S]-</header>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<footer[^>]*>[%s%S]-</footer>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<form[^>]*>[%s%S]-</form>", " ")
  end
  html = string.gsub(html, "<script[%s%S]-</script>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<style[%s%S]-</style>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<head[^>]*>[%s%S]-</head>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<!%-%-[%s%S]-%-%->", " ")
  -- math: keep the LaTeX alttext inline if present (position-independent),
  -- then drop the whole <math>...</math> span (LaTeXML never nests math)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<math([^>]*)>[%s%S]-</math>", function(attrs)
    local alt = string.match(attrs, 'alttext="([^"]*)"')
    if alt ~= nil then return " $" .. shared.decode_entities(alt) .. "$ " end
    return " "
  end)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<annotation[%s%S]-</annotation>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<svg[%s%S]-</svg>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<img[%s%S]->", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<br[%s%S]->", "\n")

  html = string.gsub(html, "</(%a+)[^>]->", function(tag)
    tag = string.lower(tag)
    if para_tags[tag] then return "\n\n" end
    if line_tags[tag] then return "\n" end
    return " "
  end)
  -- remaining tags stripped (lazy to first '>' — raw '>' never appears inside a tag)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<[%s%S]->", "")
  html = shared.decode_entities(html)

  html = string.gsub(html, "[ \t]+", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, " *\n *", "\n")
  html = string.gsub(html, "\n\n\n+", "\n\n")
  html = string.gsub(html, "^\n+", "")
  html = string.gsub(html, "\n+$", "")
  return html
end

-- Split text into pages of at most max_bytes, breaking at (in priority)
-- the last paragraph seam, newline, sentence end, or space in the window.
-- Returns {pages = {...}, total_chars = n}. Terminates: brk >= 1 always.
function shared.split_pages(text, max_bytes)
  local cap = max_bytes or 8192
  local pages = {}
  local pos, n = 1, #text
  while pos <= n do
    if n - pos + 1 <= cap then
      local last = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos), "^%s+", "")
      if #last > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = last end
      break
    end
    local window = string.sub(text, pos, pos + cap - 1)
    local brk = nil
    -- last paragraph seam
    local i = #window - 1
    while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
      if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" and string.sub(window, i + 1, i + 1) == "\n" then brk = i end
      i = i - 1
    end
    -- last single newline
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last sentence end
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 2 and brk == nil do
        local prev = string.sub(window, i - 1, i - 1)
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " and (prev == "." or prev == "!") then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last space
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    if brk == nil or brk < 1 then brk = cap end
    local chunk = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos, pos + brk - 1), "%s+$", "")
    if #chunk > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = chunk end
    pos = pos + brk
    while pos <= n do
      local c = string.sub(text, pos, pos)
      if c == "\n" or c == " " or c == "\t" then pos = pos + 1 else break end
    end
  end
  if #pages == 0 then pages[1] = "" end
  return { pages = pages, total_chars = n }
end

-- Load a JSON-array state key defensively (nil/""/invalid → fallback).
function shared.load_json_state(ctx, key, fallback)
  local raw = ctx.package.get_state(key)
  if raw == nil or raw == "" or raw == "***" then return fallback end
  local ok, v = pcall(json.decode_safe, raw)
  if not ok or type(v) ~= "table" then return fallback end
  return v
end

-- The library index lives in state as a JSON object keyed by arxiv id.
function shared.load_library(ctx)
  local lib = shared.load_json_state(ctx, "library", {})
  return lib
end

-- Delete all filespace artifacts of a cached paper (library entry shape).
function shared.remove_files(ctx, sid, entry)
  local n = tonumber(entry.pages) or 0
  for i = 1, n do
    ctx.fs.delete(string.format("%s-p%03d.txt", sid, i))
  end
  ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".meta.json")
  if entry.has_pdf then ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".pdf") end
end


-- cache list: everything in the local reading library.
function run(ctx)
  local lib = shared.load_library(ctx)
  local arr = {}
  for _, entry in pairs(lib) do
    arr[#arr + 1] = {
      id = entry.id, title = entry.title, mode = entry.mode,
      pages = entry.pages, total_chars = entry.total_chars,
      published = entry.published, has_pdf = entry.has_pdf or false,
      cached_at = entry.cached_at
    }
  end
  table.sort(arr, function(x, y) return tostring(x.id) < tostring(y.id) end)
  return {success = true, count = #arr, library = arr}
end

--

-- below uses [%s%S] (matches everything) with lazy `-%b-` semantics.

local shared = {}

shared.UA = "animus-arxiv-package/0.1.0 (agent reading cache; contact via arxiv user)"
shared.API = "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query"
shared.HTML_BASE = "https://arxiv.org/html/"
shared.PDF_BASE = "https://arxiv.org/pdf/"

function shared.headers()
  return { ["User-Agent"] = shared.UA }
end

-- Old-style ids contain '/' (hep-th/9901001) — the fs namespace is slug-only.
function shared.safe_id(id)
  return string.gsub(tostring(id), "/", "_")
end

-- Error string for a failed HTTP result. A bare status hides the transport
-- reason: r.error carries curl's verdict; without it a stall reads as a
-- meaningless "HTTP 0" (alpaca Sept 14 lesson, shared blood).
function shared.http_error(r)
  local s = "HTTP " .. tostring(r.status)
  if r.error ~= nil and r.error ~= "" then
    s = s .. " (" .. tostring(r.error) .. ")"
  end
  return s
end

-- HTML entity decode: the named set plus numeric forms. utf8.char may be
-- absent in the sandbox (defensively guarded); numeric entities then fall
-- through undecoded — readable, not pretty.
function shared.decode_entities(s)
  if s == nil then return "" end
  s = string.gsub(s, "&", "&")
  s = string.gsub(s, "<", "<")
  s = string.gsub(s, ">", ">")
  s = string.gsub(s, """, '"')
  s = string.gsub(s, "'", "'")
  s = string.gsub(s, "'", "'")
  s = string.gsub(s, " ", " ")
  if utf8 ~= nil and utf8.char ~= nil then
    s = string.gsub(s, "&#x(%x+);", function(h) return utf8.char(tonumber(h, 16)) end)

end

  v = string.gsub(v, "^%s", "")

  return shared.decode_entities(v)
end

-- Parse an arXiv Atom feed into entries:
-- {id, title, authors[], summary, published, pdf_url, categories[], primary_category, abs_url}
function shared.atom_parse(xml)
  local entries = {}
  if xml == nil then return entries end
  for block in string.gmatch(xml, "<entry>[%s%S]-</entry>") do
    local e = {}
    local raw_id = shared.tag(block, "id") or ""
    e.id = string.match(raw_id, "/abs/([^%s]+)") or raw_id
    e.title = shared.tag(block, "title") or ""
    e.authors = {}
    for name in string.gmatch(block, "<name>([%s%S]-)</name>") do
      table.insert(e.authors, shared.decode_entities(string.gsub(name, "%s+", " ")))
    end
    e.summary = shared.tag(block, "summary") or ""
    local pub = string.match(block, "<published>([^<]+)</published>")
    e.published = pub and string.sub(pub, 1, 10) or ""
    e.pdf_url = nil
    for href in string.gmatch(block, '<link[^>]-title="pdf"[^>]-href="([^"]*)"') do
      e.pdf_url = href
    end
    for href in string.gmatch(block, '<link[^>]-href="([^"]*)"[^>]-title="pdf"') do
      e.pdf_url = href
    end
    e.categories = {}
    for term in string.gmatch(block, '<category term="([^"]*)"') do
      table.insert(e.categories, term)
    end
    e.primary_category = string.match(block, 'primary_category term="([^"]*)"')
      or (e.categories[1] or "")
    e.abs_url = "https://arxiv.org/abs/" .. e.id
    table.insert(entries, e)
  end
  return entries
end

-- Compact an entry for tool results: full identity, trimmed summary.
function shared.compact(e, summary_chars)
  local limit = summary_chars or 400
  local authors = {}
  for i = 1, math.min(3, #e.authors) do authors[i] = e.authors[i] end
  if #e.authors > 3 then authors[#authors + 1] = "et al." end
  local summary = e.summary or ""
  if #summary > limit then summary = string.sub(summary, 1, limit) .. "…" end
  return {
    id = e.id, title = e.title, authors = authors, published = e.published,
    primary_category = e.primary_category, summary = summary, pdf_url = e.pdf_url
  }
end

-- Compile an agent-supplied query into arXiv search syntax.
-- Expert mode: any field prefix (cat:, ti:, abs:, all:…), boolean
-- operator, or parenthesis → VERBATIM passthrough. Fixes the cat: bug
-- (Buffett field report #1): 'cat:q-fin.CP' wrapped as all:cat:q-fin.CP
-- → HTTP 400.
-- Simple mode: terms and quoted phrases AND-joined as all: fields.
-- Fixes the silent-OR bug (Buffett #2): arXiv rewrites space-separated
-- terms as implicit OR — 'sovereign default credit supply' returned the
-- latest-indexed papers from random fields (feed-echo witness:
-- 'all:sovereign OR all:default OR all:credit OR all:supply'). AND is
-- the overwhelming intent; OR stays available via expert mode.
function shared.compile_query(query)
  query = tostring(query)
  local expert = string.find(query, ":", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, " AND ", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, " OR ", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, "ANDNOT", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, "(", 1, true) ~= nil
  if expert then return query end
  local terms = {}
  local rest = string.gsub(query, '"([^"]*)"', function(p)
    if #p > 0 then terms[#terms + 1] = 'all:"' .. p .. '"' end
    return " "
  end)
  for w in string.gmatch(rest, "%S+") do
    terms[#terms + 1] = "all:" .. w
  end
  return table.concat(terms, " AND ")
end

-- The feed's own <title> echoes the query the API actually executed
-- ('arXiv Query: search_query=…'). Surfacing it in results makes any
-- server-side query rewrite VISIBLE — the observability that would
-- have made the silent-OR bug self-evident.
function shared.feed_query(xml)
  if xml == nil then return nil end
  local t = shared.tag(xml, "title")
  if t == nil then return nil end
  local q = string.match(t, "search_query=(.-)&id_list")
  if q == nil then q = string.match(t, "search_query=(.*)") end
  return q
end

-- URL-encode a compiled query: space → '+' (arXiv's separator form),
-- everything outside unreserved (+ and " exempt) percent-encoded.
function shared.query_url(query, start, max_results, sort)
  local compiled = shared.compile_query(query)
  local esc = string.gsub(compiled, " ", "+")
  esc = string.gsub(esc, '([^%w%-%.%_%~%+"])', function(c)
    return string.format("%%%02X", string.byte(c))
  end)
  local url = shared.API .. "?search_query=" .. esc ..
    "&start=" .. tostring(start or 0) ..
    "&max_results=" .. tostring(max_results or 10)
  if sort ~= nil and sort ~= "" then
    url = url .. "&sortBy=" .. tostring(sort) .. "&sortOrder=descending"
  end
  return url
end

function shared.id_url(id)
  local esc = string.gsub(tostring(id), "([^%w%-%.%_%~])", function(c)
    return string.format("%%%02X", string.byte(c))
  end)
  return shared.API .. "?id_list=" .. esc .. "&max_results=1"
end

-- Block-close tag classification for strip_html.
local para_tags = { p = true, div = true, section = true, article = true,
  figure = true, table = true, blockquote = true, figcaption = true,
  ul = true, ol = true, dt = true, dd = true }
for i = 1, 6 do para_tags["h" .. i] = true end
local line_tags = { li = true, tr = true, td = true, th = true }

-- HTML → text. LaTeXML renderings: math alttext kept inline as $...$ LaTeX
-- (agents read LaTeX better than stripped glyphs), script/style/head and
-- comments dropped, block closes become paragraph breaks, entities decoded.
function shared.strip_html(html)

  -- arXiv LaTeXML renderings wrap the paper in exactly ONE <article> span;
  -- everything outside it is site chrome (report-issue forms, banners,
  -- nav, footers — the live 2607 page carried more than the fixture did).
  -- Prefer the article span; fall back to explicit chrome-block removal.
  local art = string.match(html, "<article[^>]*>[%s%S]-</article>")
  if art ~= nil then
    html = art
  else
    html = string.gsub(html, "<nav[^>]*>[%s%S]-</nav>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<header[^>]*>[%s%S]-</header>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<footer[^>]*>[%s%S]-</footer>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<form[^>]*>[%s%S]-</form>", " ")
  end
  html = string.gsub(html, "<script[%s%S]-</script>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<style[%s%S]-</style>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<head[^>]*>[%s%S]-</head>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<!%-%-[%s%S]-%-%->", " ")

  -- then drop the whole <math>...</math> span (LaTeXML never nests math)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<math([^>]*)>[%s%S]-</math>", function(attrs)
    local alt = string.match(attrs, 'alttext="([^"]*)"')
    if alt ~= nil then return " $" .. shared.decode_entities(alt) .. "$ " end
    return " "
  end)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<annotation[%s%S]-</annotation>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<svg[%s%S]-</svg>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<img[%s%S]->", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<br[%s%S]->", "\n")

    if line_tags[tag] then return "\n" end
    return " "
  end)

  html = string.gsub(html, "<[%s%S]->", "")
  html = shared.decode_entities(html)

  return html

-- Split text into pages of at most max_bytes, breaking at (in priority)
-- the last paragraph seam, newline, sentence end, or space in the window.
-- Returns {pages = {...}, total_chars = n}. Terminates: brk >= 1 always.
function shared.split_pages(text, max_bytes)
  local cap = max_bytes or 8192
  local pages = {}
  local pos, n = 1, #text
  while pos <= n do
    if n - pos + 1 <= cap then
      local last = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos), "^%s+", "")
      if #last > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = last end
      break
    end
    local window = string.sub(text, pos, pos + cap - 1)
    local brk = nil
    -- last paragraph seam
    local i = #window - 1
    while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
      if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" and string.sub(window, i + 1, i + 1) == "\n" then brk = i end
      i = i - 1
    end
    -- last single newline
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last sentence end
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 2 and brk == nil do
        local prev = string.sub(window, i - 1, i - 1)
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " and (prev == "." or prev == "!") then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end

      end

    if #chunk > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = chunk end
    pos = pos + brk
    while pos <= n do
      local c = string.sub(text, pos, pos)
      if c == "\n" or c == " " or c == "\t" then pos = pos + 1 else break end
    end
  end
  if #pages == 0 then pages[1] = "" end
  return { pages = pages, total_chars = n }
end

-- Load a JSON-array state key defensively (nil/""/invalid → fallback).
function shared.load_json_state(ctx, key, fallback)
  local raw = ctx.package.get_state(key)
  if raw == nil or raw == "" or raw == "***" then return fallback end
  local ok, v = pcall(json.decode_safe, raw)
  if not ok or type(v) ~= "table" then return fallback end

end

-- The library index lives in state as a JSON object keyed by arxiv id.
function shared.load_library(ctx)
  local lib = shared.load_json_state(ctx, "library", {})
  return lib
end

-- Delete all filespace artifacts of a cached paper (library entry shape).
function shared.remove_files(ctx, sid, entry)
  local n = tonumber(entry.pages) or 0
  for i = 1, n do
    ctx.fs.delete(string.format("%s-p%03d.txt", sid, i))
  end
  ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".meta.json")
  if entry.has_pdf then ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".pdf") end
end


-- cache remove: delete a paper's pages, meta, and optional pdf from the
-- filespace, and drop it from the library index.
function run(ctx)
  local a = ctx.args
  if a.id == nil or a.id == "" then
    return {success = false, error = "id required (e.g. 2401.12345)"}
  end
  local lib = shared.load_library(ctx)
  local key = a.id
  local entry = lib[key]
  if entry == nil then
    for k, v in pairs(lib) do
      if string.sub(k, 1, #a.id) == a.id then key = k; entry = v; break end
    end
  end
  if entry == nil then
    return {success = false, error = "not cached: '" .. tostring(a.id) .. "'"}
  end
  shared.remove_files(ctx, shared.safe_id(entry.id), entry)
  lib[key] = nil
  local ok, err = ctx.package.set_state("library", json.encode(lib))
  if not ok then
    return {success = false, error = "library persist failed: " .. tostring(err)}
  end
  return {success = true, removed = key, pages_removed = tonumber(entry.pages) or 0}
end

function shared.http_error(r)
  local s = "HTTP " .. tostring(r.status)
  if r.error ~= nil and r.error ~= "" then
    s = s .. " (" .. tostring(r.error) .. ")"
  end
  return s

-- HTML entity decode: the named set plus numeric forms. utf8.char may be
-- absent in the sandbox (defensively guarded); numeric entities then fall
-- through undecoded — readable, not pretty.
function shared.decode_entities(s)
  if s == nil then return "" end
  s = string.gsub(s, "&", "&")
  s = string.gsub(s, "<", "<")
  s = string.gsub(s, ">", ">")
  s = string.gsub(s, """, '"')
  s = string.gsub(s, "'", "'")
  s = string.gsub(s, "'", "'")
  s = string.gsub(s, " ", " ")
  if utf8 ~= nil and utf8.char ~= nil then
    s = string.gsub(s, "&#x(%x+);", function(h) return utf8.char(tonumber(h, 16)) end)
    s = string.gsub(s, "&#(%d+);", function(d) return utf8.char(tonumber(d)) end)
  end
  return s
end

-- Tag inner text (title/summary span lines; tolerate line-broken markup).
function shared.tag(block, name)
  local v = string.match(block, "<" .. name .. "[^>]*>[%s%S]-</" .. name .. ">")
  if v == nil then return nil end
  v = string.gsub(v, "^<" .. name .. "[^>]*>", "")
  v = string.gsub(v, "</" .. name .. ">$", "")
  v = string.gsub(v, "<[^>]*>", "")
  v = string.gsub(v, "%s+", " ")
  v = string.gsub(v, "^%s", "")
  v = string.gsub(v, "%s$", "")
  return shared.decode_entities(v)
end

-- Parse an arXiv Atom feed into entries:
-- {id, title, authors[], summary, published, pdf_url, categories[], primary_category, abs_url}
function shared.atom_parse(xml)
  local entries = {}
  if xml == nil then return entries end
  for block in string.gmatch(xml, "<entry>[%s%S]-</entry>") do
    local e = {}
    local raw_id = shared.tag(block, "id") or ""
    e.id = string.match(raw_id, "/abs/([^%s]+)") or raw_id
    e.title = shared.tag(block, "title") or ""
    e.authors = {}
    for name in string.gmatch(block, "<name>([%s%S]-)</name>") do
      table.insert(e.authors, shared.decode_entities(string.gsub(name, "%s+", " ")))
    end
    e.summary = shared.tag(block, "summary") or ""
    local pub = string.match(block, "<published>([^<]+)</published>")
    e.published = pub and string.sub(pub, 1, 10) or ""
    e.pdf_url = nil
    for href in string.gmatch(block, '<link[^>]-title="pdf"[^>]-href="([^"]*)"') do
      e.pdf_url = href
    end
    for href in string.gmatch(block, '<link[^>]-href="([^"]*)"[^>]-title="pdf"') do
      e.pdf_url = href
    end
    e.categories = {}
    for term in string.gmatch(block, '<category term="([^"]*)"') do
      table.insert(e.categories, term)
    end
    e.primary_category = string.match(block, 'primary_category term="([^"]*)"')
      or (e.categories[1] or "")

  local limit = summary_chars or 400

  if #e.authors > 3 then authors[#authors + 1] = "et al." end
  local summary = e.summary or ""
  if #summary > limit then summary = string.sub(summary, 1, limit) .. "…" end
  return {

-- Compile an agent-supplied query into arXiv search syntax.
-- Expert mode: any field prefix (cat:, ti:, abs:, all:…), boolean
-- operator, or parenthesis → VERBATIM passthrough. Fixes the cat: bug
-- (Buffett field report #1): 'cat:q-fin.CP' wrapped as all:cat:q-fin.CP
-- → HTTP 400.
-- Simple mode: terms and quoted phrases AND-joined as all: fields.
-- Fixes the silent-OR bug (Buffett #2): arXiv rewrites space-separated
-- terms as implicit OR — 'sovereign default credit supply' returned the
-- latest-indexed papers from random fields (feed-echo witness:
-- 'all:sovereign OR all:default OR all:credit OR all:supply'). AND is
-- the overwhelming intent; OR stays available via expert mode.
function shared.compile_query(query)
  query = tostring(query)
  local expert = string.find(query, ":", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, " AND ", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, " OR ", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, "ANDNOT", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, "(", 1, true) ~= nil
  if expert then return query end
  local terms = {}
  local rest = string.gsub(query, '"([^"]*)"', function(p)
    if #p > 0 then terms[#terms + 1] = 'all:"' .. p .. '"' end
    return " "
  end)
  for w in string.gmatch(rest, "%S+") do
    terms[#terms + 1] = "all:" .. w
  end
  return table.concat(terms, " AND ")
end

-- ('arXiv Query: search_query=…'). Surfacing it in results makes any
-- server-side query rewrite VISIBLE — the observability that would
-- have made the silent-OR bug self-evident.
function shared.feed_query(xml)
  if xml == nil then return nil end
  local t = shared.tag(xml, "title")
  if t == nil then return nil end
  local q = string.match(t, "search_query=(.-)&id_list")
  if q == nil then q = string.match(t, "search_query=(.*)") end
  return q

-- everything outside unreserved (+ and " exempt) percent-encoded.

  local esc = string.gsub(compiled, " ", "+")
  esc = string.gsub(esc, '([^%w%-%.%_%~%+"])', function(c)
    return string.format("%%%02X", string.byte(c))
  end)
  local url = shared.API .. "?search_query=" .. esc ..

  if sort ~= nil and sort ~= "" then

  return url

-- Block-close tag classification for strip_html.
local para_tags = { p = true, div = true, section = true, article = true,
  figure = true, table = true, blockquote = true, figcaption = true,
  ul = true, ol = true, dt = true, dd = true }
for i = 1, 6 do para_tags["h" .. i] = true end
local line_tags = { li = true, tr = true, td = true, th = true }

-- HTML → text. LaTeXML renderings: math alttext kept inline as $...$ LaTeX
-- (agents read LaTeX better than stripped glyphs), script/style/head and
-- comments dropped, block closes become paragraph breaks, entities decoded.
function shared.strip_html(html)
  if html == nil then return "" end
  -- arXiv LaTeXML renderings wrap the paper in exactly ONE <article> span;
  -- everything outside it is site chrome (report-issue forms, banners,
  -- nav, footers — the live 2607 page carried more than the fixture did).
  -- Prefer the article span; fall back to explicit chrome-block removal.
  local art = string.match(html, "<article[^>]*>[%s%S]-</article>")
  if art ~= nil then
    html = art
  else
    html = string.gsub(html, "<nav[^>]*>[%s%S]-</nav>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<header[^>]*>[%s%S]-</header>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<footer[^>]*>[%s%S]-</footer>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<form[^>]*>[%s%S]-</form>", " ")
  end
  html = string.gsub(html, "<script[%s%S]-</script>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<style[%s%S]-</style>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<head[^>]*>[%s%S]-</head>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<!%-%-[%s%S]-%-%->", " ")
  -- math: keep the LaTeX alttext inline if present (position-independent),
  -- then drop the whole <math>...</math> span (LaTeXML never nests math)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<math([^>]*)>[%s%S]-</math>", function(attrs)
    local alt = string.match(attrs, 'alttext="([^"]*)"')
    if alt ~= nil then return " $" .. shared.decode_entities(alt) .. "$ " end
    return " "
  end)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<annotation[%s%S]-</annotation>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<svg[%s%S]-</svg>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<img[%s%S]->", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<br[%s%S]->", "\n")
  -- block closes → breaks (before generic strip; inserted text has no '<')
  html = string.gsub(html, "</(%a+)[^>]->", function(tag)
    tag = string.lower(tag)
    if para_tags[tag] then return "\n\n" end
    if line_tags[tag] then return "\n" end
    return " "
  end)
  -- remaining tags stripped (lazy to first '>' — raw '>' never appears inside a tag)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<[%s%S]->", "")
  html = shared.decode_entities(html)
  -- collapse: space runs → one; blank-line runs → one blank line; trim ends
  html = string.gsub(html, "[ \t]+", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, " *\n *", "\n")
  html = string.gsub(html, "\n\n\n+", "\n\n")
  html = string.gsub(html, "^\n+", "")
  html = string.gsub(html, "\n+$", "")
  return html
end

-- Split text into pages of at most max_bytes, breaking at (in priority)
-- the last paragraph seam, newline, sentence end, or space in the window.
-- Returns {pages = {...}, total_chars = n}. Terminates: brk >= 1 always.
function shared.split_pages(text, max_bytes)
  local cap = max_bytes or 8192
  local pages = {}
  local pos, n = 1, #text
  while pos <= n do
    if n - pos + 1 <= cap then
      local last = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos), "^%s+", "")
      if #last > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = last end
      break
    end
    local window = string.sub(text, pos, pos + cap - 1)
    local brk = nil
    -- last paragraph seam
    local i = #window - 1
    while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
      if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" and string.sub(window, i + 1, i + 1) == "\n" then brk = i end
      i = i - 1
    end
    -- last single newline
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last sentence end
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 2 and brk == nil do
        local prev = string.sub(window, i - 1, i - 1)
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " and (prev == "." or prev == "!") then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last space
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    if brk == nil or brk < 1 then brk = cap end
    local chunk = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos, pos + brk - 1), "%s+$", "")
    if #chunk > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = chunk end
    pos = pos + brk
    while pos <= n do
      local c = string.sub(text, pos, pos)
      if c == "\n" or c == " " or c == "\t" then pos = pos + 1 else break end
    end
  end
  if #pages == 0 then pages[1] = "" end
  return { pages = pages, total_chars = n }
end

-- Load a JSON-array state key defensively (nil/""/invalid → fallback).
function shared.load_json_state(ctx, key, fallback)
  local raw = ctx.package.get_state(key)
  if raw == nil or raw == "" or raw == "***" then return fallback end
  local ok, v = pcall(json.decode_safe, raw)
  if not ok or type(v) ~= "table" then return fallback end
  return v
end

-- The library index lives in state as a JSON object keyed by arxiv id.
function shared.load_library(ctx)
  local lib = shared.load_json_state(ctx, "library", {})
  return lib
end

-- Delete all filespace artifacts of a cached paper (library entry shape).
function shared.remove_files(ctx, sid, entry)
  local n = tonumber(entry.pages) or 0
  for i = 1, n do
    ctx.fs.delete(string.format("%s-p%03d.txt", sid, i))
  end
  ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".meta.json")
  if entry.has_pdf then ctx.fs.delete(sid .. ".pdf") end
end


-- poll: new-paper check. With a 'phrase' arg, queries that phrase once
-- (rotation state untouched); otherwise rotates through the configured
-- list, one phrase per invocation. Politeness by construction: the
-- sandbox has no sleep, so the caller's cadence is the throttle (arXiv
-- asks for >= 3s between queries — schedule this no tighter than one
-- call per few minutes). New ids are recorded in 'seen' (capped at the
-- most recent 1000) and returned for the agent to triage; nothing is
-- ever auto-cached.
function run(ctx)
  local a = ctx.args or {}
  local phrases = shared.load_json_state(ctx, "phrases", {})
  local phrase, cursor, rotating
  if a.phrase ~= nil and tostring(a.phrase) ~= "" then
    phrase = tostring(a.phrase)
    rotating = false
  else
    if #phrases == 0 then
      return {success = false,
              error = "no phrases configured — use the 'phrases add' command, or pass a 'phrase' arg for a one-off check",
              state_key = "phrases"}
    end
    cursor = tonumber(ctx.package.get_state("poll_cursor")) or 0
    phrase = phrases[(cursor % #phrases) + 1]
    rotating = true
  end

  local r = ctx.http.get(shared.query_url(phrase, 0, 5, "submittedDate"),
                         {headers = shared.headers()})
  if r.status ~= 200 then
    return {success = false, error = "poll query failed: " .. shared.http_error(r),
            phrase = phrase}
  end
  local entries = shared.atom_parse(r.body)

  local seen = shared.load_json_state(ctx, "seen", {})
  local set = {}
  for _, v in ipairs(seen) do set[v] = true end
  local new = {}
  for _, e in ipairs(entries) do
    if not set[e.id] then
      set[e.id] = true
      seen[#seen + 1] = e.id
      new[#new + 1] = shared.compact(e)
    end
  end
  while #seen > 1000 do table.remove(seen, 1) end

  local ok, err = ctx.package.set_state("seen", json.encode(seen))
  if not ok then return {success = false, error = "seen persist failed: " .. tostring(err)} end

  local out = {
    success = true, phrase = phrase,
    executed_query = shared.feed_query(r.body),
    returned = #entries, new_count = #new, new_papers = new
  }
  if rotating then
    ok, err = ctx.package.set_state("poll_cursor", tostring(cursor + 1))
    if not ok then return {success = false, error = "cursor persist failed: " .. tostring(err)} end
    out.next_phrase = phrases[((cursor + 1) % #phrases) + 1]
  end
  return out
end

function shared.strip_html(html)
  if html == nil then return "" end
  -- arXiv LaTeXML renderings wrap the paper in exactly ONE <article> span;
  -- everything outside it is site chrome (report-issue forms, banners,
  -- nav, footers — the live 2607 page carried more than the fixture did).
  -- Prefer the article span; fall back to explicit chrome-block removal.
  local art = string.match(html, "<article[^>]*>[%s%S]-</article>")
  if art ~= nil then
    html = art
  else
    html = string.gsub(html, "<nav[^>]*>[%s%S]-</nav>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<header[^>]*>[%s%S]-</header>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<footer[^>]*>[%s%S]-</footer>", " ")
    html = string.gsub(html, "<form[^>]*>[%s%S]-</form>", " ")
  end
  html = string.gsub(html, "<script[%s%S]-</script>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<style[%s%S]-</style>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<head[^>]*>[%s%S]-</head>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<!%-%-[%s%S]-%-%->", " ")
  -- math: keep the LaTeX alttext inline if present (position-independent),
  -- then drop the whole <math>...</math> span (LaTeXML never nests math)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<math([^>]*)>[%s%S]-</math>", function(attrs)

    return " "
  end)
  html = string.gsub(html, "<annotation[%s%S]-</annotation>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<svg[%s%S]-</svg>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<img[%s%S]->", " ")

  html = string.gsub(html, "[ \t]+", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, " *\n *", "\n")
  html = string.gsub(html, "\n\n\n+", "\n\n")
  html = string.gsub(html, "^\n+", "")
  html = string.gsub(html, "\n+$", "")

-- Split text into pages of at most max_bytes, breaking at (in priority)
-- the last paragraph seam, newline, sentence end, or space in the window.
-- Returns {pages = {...}, total_chars = n}. Terminates: brk >= 1 always.
function shared.split_pages(text, max_bytes)
  local cap = max_bytes or 8192
  local pages = {}
  local pos, n = 1, #text
  while pos <= n do
    if n - pos + 1 <= cap then
      local last = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos), "^%s+", "")
      if #last > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = last end
      break
    end
    local window = string.sub(text, pos, pos + cap - 1)
    local brk = nil
    -- last paragraph seam
    local i = #window - 1
    while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
      if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" and string.sub(window, i + 1, i + 1) == "\n" then brk = i end
      i = i - 1
    end
    -- last single newline
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last sentence end
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 2 and brk == nil do
        local prev = string.sub(window, i - 1, i - 1)
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " and (prev == "." or prev == "!") then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last space
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    if brk == nil or brk < 1 then brk = cap end
    local chunk = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos, pos + brk - 1), "%s+$", "")
    if #chunk > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = chunk end
    pos = pos + brk
    while pos <= n do
      local c = string.sub(text, pos, pos)
      if c == "\n" or c == " " or c == "\t" then pos = pos + 1 else break end
    end
  end
  if #pages == 0 then pages[1] = "" end
  return { pages = pages, total_chars = n }
end

function shared.load_json_state(ctx, key, fallback)
  local raw = ctx.package.get_state(key)
  if raw == nil or raw == "" or raw == "***" then return fallback end
  local ok, v = pcall(json.decode_safe, raw)
  if not ok or type(v) ~= "table" then return fallback end

end

function shared.load_library(ctx)

end

-- Delete all filespace artifacts of a cached paper (library entry shape).
function shared.remove_files(ctx, sid, entry)
  local n = tonumber(entry.pages) or 0
  for i = 1, n do
    ctx.fs.delete(string.format("%s-p%03d.txt", sid, i))
  end

-- Agent self-configuration — no admin state access needed.
function run(ctx)
  local a = ctx.args
  if a.phrase == nil or a.phrase == "" then
    return {success = false, error = "phrase required"}
  end
  local phrases = shared.load_json_state(ctx, "phrases", {})
  for _, p in ipairs(phrases) do
    if p == a.phrase then
      return {success = false, error = "already in rotation", phrase = a.phrase,
              rotation = phrases}
    end

  phrases[#phrases + 1] = tostring(a.phrase)
  local ok, err = ctx.package.set_state("phrases", json.encode(phrases))
  if not ok then
    return {success = false, error = "phrases persist failed: " .. tostring(err)}
  end
  return {success = true, added = a.phrase, rotation_size = #phrases,
          rotation = phrases}
end

    local pub = string.match(block, "<published>([^<]+)</published>")

    e.pdf_url = nil
    for href in string.gmatch(block, '<link[^>]-title="pdf"[^>]-href="([^"]*)"') do
      e.pdf_url = href

      e.pdf_url = href
    end

    for term in string.gmatch(block, '<category term="([^"]*)"') do
      table.insert(e.categories, term)
    end

      or (e.categories[1] or "")

  end
  return entries

function shared.compact(e, summary_chars)
  local limit = summary_chars or 400
  local authors = {}
  for i = 1, math.min(3, #e.authors) do authors[i] = e.authors[i] end
  if #e.authors > 3 then authors[#authors + 1] = "et al." end
  local summary = e.summary or ""
  if #summary > limit then summary = string.sub(summary, 1, limit) .. "…" end
  return {
    id = e.id, title = e.title, authors = authors, published = e.published,

  }
end

-- Compile an agent-supplied query into arXiv search syntax.
-- Expert mode: any field prefix (cat:, ti:, abs:, all:…), boolean
-- operator, or parenthesis → VERBATIM passthrough. Fixes the cat: bug
-- (Buffett field report #1): 'cat:q-fin.CP' wrapped as all:cat:q-fin.CP
-- → HTTP 400.
-- Simple mode: terms and quoted phrases AND-joined as all: fields.
-- Fixes the silent-OR bug (Buffett #2): arXiv rewrites space-separated
-- terms as implicit OR — 'sovereign default credit supply' returned the
-- latest-indexed papers from random fields (feed-echo witness:
-- 'all:sovereign OR all:default OR all:credit OR all:supply'). AND is
-- the overwhelming intent; OR stays available via expert mode.
function shared.compile_query(query)
  query = tostring(query)
  local expert = string.find(query, ":", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, " AND ", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, " OR ", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, "ANDNOT", 1, true) ~= nil
    or string.find(query, "(", 1, true) ~= nil
  if expert then return query end
  local terms = {}
  local rest = string.gsub(query, '"([^"]*)"', function(p)
    if #p > 0 then terms[#terms + 1] = 'all:"' .. p .. '"' end
    return " "
  end)
  for w in string.gmatch(rest, "%S+") do
    terms[#terms + 1] = "all:" .. w
  end
  return table.concat(terms, " AND ")
end

-- ('arXiv Query: search_query=…'). Surfacing it in results makes any
-- server-side query rewrite VISIBLE — the observability that would
-- have made the silent-OR bug self-evident.
function shared.feed_query(xml)
  if xml == nil then return nil end
  local t = shared.tag(xml, "title")
  if t == nil then return nil end
  local q = string.match(t, "search_query=(.-)&id_list")
  if q == nil then q = string.match(t, "search_query=(.*)") end
  return q
end

-- URL-encode a compiled query: space → '+' (arXiv's separator form),
-- everything outside unreserved (+ and " exempt) percent-encoded.
function shared.query_url(query, start, max_results, sort)
  local compiled = shared.compile_query(query)
  local esc = string.gsub(compiled, " ", "+")
  esc = string.gsub(esc, '([^%w%-%.%_%~%+"])', function(c)
    return string.format("%%%02X", string.byte(c))
  end)
  local url = shared.API .. "?search_query=" .. esc ..
    "&start=" .. tostring(start or 0) ..
    "&max_results=" .. tostring(max_results or 10)
  if sort ~= nil and sort ~= "" then
    url = url .. "&sortBy=" .. tostring(sort) .. "&sortOrder=descending"
  end
  return url
end

function shared.id_url(id)
  local esc = string.gsub(tostring(id), "([^%w%-%.%_%~])", function(c)
    return string.format("%%%02X", string.byte(c))
  end)
  return shared.API .. "?id_list=" .. esc .. "&max_results=1"

-- Block-close tag classification for strip_html.
local para_tags = { p = true, div = true, section = true, article = true,
  figure = true, table = true, blockquote = true, figcaption = true,
  ul = true, ol = true, dt = true, dd = true }

-- comments dropped, block closes become paragraph breaks, entities decoded.
function shared.strip_html(html)

  -- arXiv LaTeXML renderings wrap the paper in exactly ONE <article> span;
  -- everything outside it is site chrome (report-issue forms, banners,
  -- nav, footers — the live 2607 page carried more than the fixture did).
  -- Prefer the article span; fall back to explicit chrome-block removal.
  local art = string.match(html, "<article[^>]*>[%s%S]-</article>")

    html = string.gsub(html, "<header[^>]*>[%s%S]-</header>", " ")

  html = string.gsub(html, "<style[%s%S]-</style>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<head[^>]*>[%s%S]-</head>", " ")

  html = string.gsub(html, "<svg[%s%S]-</svg>", " ")
  html = string.gsub(html, "<img[%s%S]->", " ")

-- the last paragraph seam, newline, sentence end, or space in the window.
-- Returns {pages = {...}, total_chars = n}. Terminates: brk >= 1 always.

    if n - pos + 1 <= cap then
      local last = string.gsub(string.sub(text, pos), "^%s+", "")
      if #last > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = last end
      break
    end
    local window = string.sub(text, pos, pos + cap - 1)
    local brk = nil
    -- last paragraph seam
    local i = #window - 1
    while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
      if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" and string.sub(window, i + 1, i + 1) == "\n" then brk = i end
      i = i - 1
    end
    -- last single newline
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 1 and brk == nil do
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == "\n" then brk = i end
        i = i - 1
      end
    end
    -- last sentence end
    if brk == nil then
      i = #window
      while i >= 2 and brk == nil do
        local prev = string.sub(window, i - 1, i - 1)
        if string.sub(window, i, i) == " " and (prev == "." or prev == "!") then brk = i end

      end
    end

    if #chunk > 0 then pages[#pages + 1] = chunk end
    pos = pos + brk
    while pos <= n do
      local c = string.sub(text, pos, pos)
      if c == "\n" or c == " " or c == "\t" then pos = pos + 1 else break end
    end
  end
  if #pages == 0 then pages[1] = "" end
  return { pages = pages, total_chars = n }
end

-- Load a JSON-array state key defensively (nil/""/invalid → fallback).
function shared.load_json_state(ctx, key, fallback)
  local raw = ctx.package.get_state(key)
